record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: If finitely presented ℓ-groups satisfy the same first order sentences, must they be isomorphic?

evidence.quote: 1.54. (G. Sabbagh) If finitely presented ℓ-groups satisfy the same first order sentences, must they be isomorphic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is an algebraic structure (G, ·, ⁻¹, e, ∧, ∨) such that (G, ·, ⁻¹, e) is a group, (G, ∧, ∨) is a lattice, and the group multiplication distributes over both lattice operations on the left and on the right; that is, for all a, b, c, d ∈ G, a(b ∨ c)d = abd ∨ acd and a(b ∧ c)d = abd ∧ acd. An ℓ-group is finitely presented if it can be presented by finitely many generators and finitely many relations in the variety of ℓ-groups. Two ℓ-groups G and H are elementarily equivalent if they satisfy exactly the same sentences in the first-order language {·, ⁻¹, e, ∧, ∨}.

Question: Must any two finitely presented ℓ-groups that are elementarily equivalent be isomorphic?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source resolving whether elementarily equivalent finitely presented ℓ-groups must be isomorphic. The analogous question for finitely generated/finitely presented groups has only been resolved in special cases (e.g., first-order rigidity for certain higher-rank arithmetic groups), and no result specifically addressing the ℓ-group version was located. The current status appears unverified from available public sources.

status_evidence.title: First order rigidity of non-uniform higher rank arithmetic groups
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes first-order rigidity for certain classes of finitely generated groups, but does not address lattice-ordered groups.
status_evidence.claim: Related rigidity results exist for groups but not for the ℓ-group version asked here.
